name: afxdp-socket
why: socket(AF_XDP=0x2c) is the express-data-path capture surface; the family alone is the signal
source: recorded: strace of afxdp_socket_behavioral.c -- socket(AF_XDP, SOCK_RAW, 0)

name: afxdp-socket-cloexec
why: socket(AF_XDP) with SOCK_RAW|SOCK_CLOEXEC (a1=0x80003) from a differently named tool is the same family chokepoint; the CLOEXEC flag bit must not hide it and comm must not matter
source: synthetic: an AF_XDP capture tool opening the socket with SOCK_CLOEXEC

name: afpacket-wrong-family
why: an AF_PACKET (0x11) raw socket is the Strategy 1 surface, not AF_XDP; the a0 family constraint must be load-bearing

name: afinet-dgram-wrong-family
why: an ordinary AF_INET (0x2) UDP socket shares the socket() syscall but not the AF_XDP family; flipping only a0 fires it
source: synthetic: a normal UDP socket open

name: setsockopt-on-fd44-not-socket
why: auditd logs socket()'s a0 as the family, but for setsockopt() a0 is the fd number; a setsockopt on fd 0x2c (44) holds the a0=0x2c atom yet is not the socket() syscall. This is the realistic high-volume look-alike in this schema, so the socket syscall anchor must be load-bearing
source: synthetic: setsockopt(SO_REUSEADDR) on fd 44 (a0 collides with the AF_XDP family value)

name: unrelated-syscall
why: an ordinary ioctl(fd, TCGETS) by a routine process: an audited syscall (atomic.rules records ioctl) that shares neither the anchored syscall nor its arguments -- a sanity floor that must stay quiet
source: synthetic: a routine ioctl(TCGETS), an audited high-volume syscall used as a non-firing floor
